newsitem.title: UK: Reuters says sterling strength hits revenue.
newsitem.headline: Reuters says sterling strength hits revenue.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc said on Wednesday that the strong pound had cut first quarter revenue by two percent to 699 million pounds ($1.1 billion).

Peter Job, chief executive of the international news and information organisation, said in a statement that if the pound remained at current levels Reuters expected to announce little or no growth in reported pre-tax profit and earnings at the half-year stage.
The profit warning pushed Reuters share price down seven pence on the day to 585p, well below the session high of 597p.
"Traders will see headlines like 'No profits growth in first half' and mark down the prices," one analyst said.
But he added that the market should not be surprised at the profit warning and that growth could be recorded in the second half "which will mean overall growth for the whole year".
Chairman Sir Christopher Hogg told shareholders at an annual general meeting that the impact of exchange rates "does not affect the fundamental business".

Both Hogg and Job said the company would like to go ahead with a share buyback to reward shareholders but that UK government restrictions were holding it back. Job told Reuters Financial Television the company faced a "forest of regulation" in implementing the buyback.
Reuters had net funds of 1.05 billion pounds at the end of 1996. Plans to return 613 million pounds to shareholders via a share buyback were thwarted last year by a change in the UK tax regulations.
These regulations "still stymie us as we see it on doing what we regard as fair to all shareholders on both sides of the Atlantic," Hogg said.
Reuters said underlying growth in first quarter revenue was eight percent up on a year earlier.
"Sterling's strength continues to have a negative impact on our reported figures," Job said.

"Meantime, the business is performing much as we expected. We mainly invoice in local currency all over the world so sterling exchange rate movements are not having any impact on unit sales," he said.

He said the company was making steady progress towards its year-end target for its new 3000 range of financial information products and said newer business lines including risk management software and business information sales to corporations were also performing steadily.
"Instinet, our electronic equities trading subsidiary, continues to do well and foreign exchange transaction revenue at comparable rates is up on last year," Job added.
But Oliver Ehrenburg, telecoms analyst at Robert Fleming, a seller of Reuters stock, said though the overall figures were as expected there were certain disappointing elements.
"Growth at Instinet, for example, which grew at 42 percent last year is now growing at nine percent whereas people were expecting 15 percent," he said.
Sterling currency conversions are at a rate of $1.63, a rate prevailing at March 31. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
